metais help json — The JSON document every command prints with --json.

With --json, a run prints exactly one JSON document on standard output: compact
UTF-8 with no byte order mark, one line ending in one LF, HTML escaping off, and
standard error empty. Its members are always present, in this order:

  format    The document's name and major version, metais.<command>/<major>.
  ok        True when the command completed and no finding is an error.
  findings  The findings, in the specification's order; [] when there are none.
            A usage error is a finding too.
  summary   The exact counts of errors, warnings and info, how many findings are
            listed and omitted, and the count of each code.
  result    The command's result, or null when it was refused before producing
            one.
  next      The commands to run next, each {"run", "why"}; [] when there is
            nothing to suggest, and never empty after a refusal.

The exit status is the same with and without --json, and --json is honoured even
on a command line that does not parse. Within a major version a format only
gains members and enumeration values: ignore a member you do not know, and read
an unknown value as other.

The formats:
  metais.inspect/1   metais inspect
  metais.ls/1        metais ls
  metais.read/1      metais read
  metais.outline/1   metais outline
  metais.grep/1      metais grep
  metais.schema/1    metais schema
  metais.extract/1   metais extract
  metais.validate/1  metais validate
  metais.init/1      metais init
  metais.check/1     metais check
  metais.unpack/1    metais unpack
  metais.version/1   metais version
  metais.limits/1    metais limits
  metais.help/1      metais help
  metais.usage/1     a line that names no command
